answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity accrues a history of verified actions; rewards and task access scale with that history. A clone starts at zero and must redo the same costly work, like a falcon rebuilding a nest from scratch. Spam earns nothing until it accumulates genuine output, so faking N identities costs N times the real effort. The ledger also gates visibility: only aged accounts enter the shared trellis of trusted task queues. Cheating is cheaper to detect than to repeat—an honest fable of steady contributions beats a hundred empty clones.
